chains.title: CTCF ref-gain at a cryptic element with distal FAM110B effect
chains.element: cryptic or condition-specific CTCF-bound element outside called cCREs

links.claim: CTCF is the only listed bound, expressed TF with a binding model at this site, chosen because E04/E05/E10 report CTCF occupancy and expression, but the only peak containing the variant is in LNCAP, not liver; no QBiC-SELEX evidence for CTCF at this base is supplied, so the hypothesis that ref G binds CTCF more strongly than alt T is speculative.

The variant is an intronic/intergenic site with no overlapping cCRE; the nearest cCRE is 1544 bp away, and the only CTCF peak containing the variant is outside liver, so any CTCF-bound element here would be cryptic or condition-specific rather than a canonical liver regulatory element.

FAM110B is the nearest protein-coding gene at 420.6 kb, but GTEx reports no significant eQTL for rs7001688 and the only literature link is a statin-response study involving FAM110B, not a direct rs7001688-to-FAM110B expression link.

CTCF is expressed in Hep3B2.1-7, but ENCODE reports no CTCF ChIP peak at this site in the HepG2 liver proxy; the chain requires hepatocyte-specific or condition-specific CTCF occupancy that is not demonstrated.

If hepatocyte CTCF binding at this cryptic element changed FAM110B expression, it could influence LDL cholesterol, but there is no rs7001688 GWAS, Open Targets, or eQTL support for this variant-to-phenotype link.

grades_v0.reason: E04/E05 show CTCF as the only listed bound, expressed TF with a model and a CTCF peak containing the variant, but only in LNCAP; there is no HepG2/liver occupancy and no QBiC-SELEX or allele-specific assay showing ref G binds more than alt T. This is at best indirect occupancy evidence for the directional binding claim.

E01/E03/E04/E05 directly support that the variant does not overlap a cCRE, the nearest cCRE is 1544 bp away, and the only CTCF peak is outside liver. This supports the stated negative/weak-element characterization, though it does not establish a functional liver element.

E02 establishes only that FAM110B is the nearest protein-coding gene at 420.6 kb; E08 shows no significant GTEx eQTL and E09 is a statin-response study, not direct evidence that rs7001688 alters FAM110B expression. This is proximity/indirect evidence, not a variant-to-gene link.

E05 supports CTCF expression in Hep3B2.1-7, and E04/E05 support absence of a HepG2 CTCF peak at this site. This shows the cell-type context is plausible but does not demonstrate the required hepatocyte-specific CTCF occupancy.

The phenotype step is explicitly speculative. E09 concerns FAM110B and statin response, not rs7001688 LDL cholesterol, and no GWAS/eQTL or perturbation evidence connects this variant to LDL via FAM110B.

E04/E05 show CTCF as the only listed bound, expressed TF with a model and a CTCF peak containing the variant in LNCAP, but not in HepG2/liver. There is no QBiC-SELEX or allele-specific assay showing alt T binds more than ref G; this is indirect and does not establish the claimed direction.

E01/E03/E04/E05 directly support that the variant lies outside a cCRE, the nearest cCRE is 1544 bp away, and the CTCF peak is non-liver. This supports the claim that any element would be cryptic/condition-specific rather than a canonical liver cCRE.

E02 establishes only that CYP7A1 is 926.8 kb downstream; E08 shows no significant GTEx eQTL and no chromatin-contact evidence is supplied. The statement that CYP7A1 is the most LDL-relevant nearby gene is external biology, not supported by the cited evidence, and the variant-to-gene link remains unproven.
